correctness.rationale: Condition on the ordered pattern of the first t transition types, not on the positions. Its k relocations generate k independent uniform starts for k+1 labelled clockwise arcs totaling t+1 sites, with the first arc anchored. For t<n, disjoint placements are in bijection with the k! orders of the other labels and weak compositions of the n-t-1 unused sites over k+1 gaps; this gives the proposed rising factorial, independent of the arc lengths. The ratio for k to k+1 is (n-t+k)/n<1 for k<t; monotone coupling of the binomial counts gives strictness for t>=1, including comparison with q=0 and q=1. For t=n the pigeonhole bound applies, not the arc count. For t=floor(nx) and finite nq, tight binomial-to-Poisson mixing yields exp(-lambda x^2) for x<1, including lambda=0. For t=n-1 the conditional factor is k!/n^k, so the mass at T=n tends to exp(-lambda). Support in [0,1] justifies convergence of the mean in this window. On t=floor(x sqrt(n/q)), x>0 and nq diverging, K/(tq) tends to one and t/n tends to zero. Summing log(1-(t-j)/n) over 0<=j<K gives -Kt/n+K(K-1)/(2n) with error O(K t^2/n^2)=o_P(1). The two terms tend to -x^2 and q_infty x^2/2, including the q_infty=0 and 1 regimes. The conditional survival factors are bounded by one, permitting averaging. x=0 is exact. This is an analytical proof; VERIFICATION.md's recorded 438 finite comparisons from checker.py were inspected as supporting evidence, not rerun or used as the limit proof. No expectation convergence in the many-relocation window is asserted.

value.rationale: First repetition measures how much of the cycle is explored without a collision. The exact finite law and its two scaling limits distinguish the survival of a full traversal with positive limiting probability from the birthday-scale cutoff.
